boston-conservatory-berklee-summer-inten.about:
Boston Conservatory at Berklee runs a set of summer intensives for serious young performers: Musical Theater Dance Intensive (ages 15–25, 13 June–2 July), Vocal/Choral Intensive (15–18, 21 June–3 July), Brass Workshop (15+, 28 June–2 July), High School Composition Intensive (15–19, 12–23 July), Commercial Dance Intensive (15–25, 12–30 July), Musical Theater Acting Intensive (15–18, 12–30 July), Summer Dance Intensive (15–22, 19 July–6 August) and a Youth Musical Theater programme for ages 12–14.

Students train daily with conservatory faculty in Boston and can live in conservatory housing. Tuition ranges from about USD 1,095 (Brass Workshop) to USD 3,280 (three-week intensives), with housing USD 895–2,720; registering by 31 January 2027 gives a discount on several programmes. The page does not set nationality limits; international students should confirm visa requirements with the conservatory.
boston-conservatory-berklee-summer-inten.eligibility: Ages vary by programme (mostly 15–18; some 15–25; youth programme 12–14). No nationality restriction is stated; international participants should confirm visa arrangements with the conservatory.
how_to_apply: Choose an intensive on the summer page
Register online (by 31 January 2027 for the early discount where offered)
Submit any audition or video material requested
Book conservatory housing and arrange travel and visa
boston-conservatory-berklee-summer-inten.costs: Tuition USD 900–3,280 depending on programme; housing USD 895–2,720. Travel and visa extra.

boston-university-summer-term-internatio.about:
Boston University Summer Term opens hundreds of regular BU courses from 12 schools and colleges to visiting students. International college students (and other adults) can earn transferable credit in subjects from business and engineering to communication and the arts, studying in person in Boston or online, and can live in BU housing.

In 2027 Session 1 runs 18 May–25 June and Session 2 28 June–6 August. Course listings appear on 17 December 2026 and the application for visiting international college students opens on 15 January 2027. BU provides visa guidance for those studying in person; international high-school students should use BU's pre-college programmes instead.
highlights: Courses from 12 BU schools and colleges
Two six-week sessions, in person or online
boston-university-summer-term-internatio.eligibility: Visiting international college students and adults (not high-school students). English proficiency required for credit courses.
how_to_apply: Browse 2027 courses from 17 December 2026
Apply as a visiting international college student from 15 January 2027
Register for courses and request visa documents early if studying in Boston
Book BU summer housing
boston-university-summer-term-internatio.costs: Tuition per credit plus fees and housing as listed on BU Summer Term's Tuition, Fees & Payment page.

boston-university-tanglewood-institute-2.about:
The Boston University Tanglewood Institute (BUTI) is a residential summer programme for talented high-school musicians, held in Lenox, Massachusetts, alongside the Tanglewood Music Festival of the Boston Symphony Orchestra. Young Artists programmes (orchestra, wind ensemble, vocal, piano, composition and others) offer full-summer training with BU faculty and BSO musicians, while shorter workshops focus on a single instrument.

In 2027 workshops run 18–30 June and Young Artists programmes 4 July–14 August. Applications open 1 November 2026 with a 15 January 2027 deadline (later applications reviewed if space remains) and an audition recording; the application fee is USD 80 (waivers for financial hardship). An optional scholarship application is part of the admission form. Students come from across the US and around the world.
highlights: Train next to the Boston Symphony Orchestra's Tanglewood Festival
Young Artists orchestra, wind ensemble and vocal programmes
Scholarship application built into the admission form
boston-university-tanglewood-institute-2.eligibility: Advanced high-school musicians (by audition). International students are accepted; they need a US visa.
how_to_apply: Choose a Young Artists programme or workshop
Apply online from 1 November 2026 and upload audition recordings
Pay the USD 80 application fee (or request a hardship waiver)
Complete the optional scholarship application
Submit by 15 January 2027; decisions before 15 March
boston-university-tanglewood-institute-2.costs: Paid residential programme; tuition listed on BUTI's tuition page. Application fee USD 80. Need- and merit-based scholarships available.

breakthrough-junior-challenge-2027.about:
The Breakthrough Junior Challenge is an annual global competition from the Breakthrough Prize Foundation (founded by technology entrepreneurs to celebrate fundamental science). Students create an original video of two minutes or less explaining a concept or theory in the physical sciences, life sciences or mathematics, aimed at a general audience, and post it publicly on YouTube.

Entrants must be 13–18 and submit in English; residents of regions under comprehensive US sanctions are excluded. After submitting, entrants peer-review other videos before judging. In 2026 the window ran 11 May–15 September; the 2027 edition is expected to follow the same timing. The winner receives a USD 250,000 college scholarship, the teacher who inspired them USD 50,000, and their school a new science lab worth up to USD 100,000 (about USD 400,000 in total).
breakthrough-junior-challenge-2027.eligibility: Students aged 13–18 (age limits set each year) from any country except those under comprehensive US sanctions. Videos in English.
how_to_apply: Pick a concept in physics, life sciences or maths
Script and record an original video of two minutes or less in English
Register on the Breakthrough Junior Challenge site when the 2027 window opens (around May)
Submit before the deadline (around mid-September) and complete peer reviews

bruinmun-34-2026.about:
BruinMUN is UCLA's high-school Model UN, now in its 34th session, with twenty-seven committees ranging from General Assembly bodies to small dual-delegate and specialised committees such as a Los Angeles Olympics City Council.

The conference runs 7–8 November 2026 at UCLA's campus, Los Angeles, United States. It is open to high school students and advisors. Working language: English.

Registration is open on the official site (advisor handbook and FAQ provided). The delegate fee is published on the official registration page. As at any MUN, delegates research their assigned country, write position papers, give speeches, negotiate in caucuses and draft resolutions — hands-on training in public speaking, research and diplomacy that universities value.
highlights: 7–8 November 2026 in Los Angeles, United States
The delegate fee is published on the official registration page
bruinmun-34-2026.eligibility: Open to high school students and advisors. Working language: English. No nationality restrictions are stated; international delegates (including from Georgia and Qatar) can apply, arranging their own visa and travel.
how_to_apply: Open the official website (link below) and read the conference information and committee list.
Registration is open on the official site (advisor handbook and FAQ provided).
Pay the delegate fee by the stated deadline to confirm your place.
Prepare a position paper using the committee study guides before the conference.
bruinmun-34-2026.costs: The delegate fee is published on the official registration page. Travel, accommodation and visas are paid by participants unless stated otherwise.

cambridge-international-summer-programme.about:
The International Summer Programme is run by the University of Cambridge's continuing-education institute and brings together learners aged 18 to 80+ from around the world. Participants study for one to four weeks (minimum one week), choosing from subject streams and over 140 courses with one or two daily lectures.

You can stay in one of five historic Cambridge colleges with breakfast and dinner included. There are no formal academic entry requirements beyond good English, making it one of the few official Cambridge summer options open to first-year students and recent school-leavers aged 18+.

The 2026 programme has ended and the 2027 programme is being prepared; register interest through the official 2027 enquiry form for dates, fees and bursaries.
cambridge-international-summer-programme.eligibility: Adults aged 18+ (no upper limit) with good English; no formal academic prerequisites.
how_to_apply: Register interest via the official 2027 contact form.
Choose weeks and courses when the 2027 programme is published.
Book online and choose college accommodation if wanted.
Pay fees and arrange a UK visitor visa if needed.
cambridge-international-summer-programme.costs: 2027 fees and bursary details to be published on the Fees page; college accommodation with breakfast and dinner optional.

cambridge-postgraduate-international-qa-.about:
Between June and December 2026, Cambridge's international admissions team hosts monthly live Q&A webinars for prospective international applicants to its Master's and PhD programmes starting in 2027 or 2028. Each session lasts about an hour on Zoom; the presentation is the same every month, so you only need to register for one.

The remaining sessions in November and December 2026 come just before many Cambridge course and funding deadlines. Recordings of the 2025 region-specific global webinar series are also available, and the team offers short online appointments for postgraduate applicants on weekdays.
highlights: Run by Cambridge's international admissions team
cambridge-postgraduate-international-qa-.eligibility: Prospective international postgraduate applicants from any country.
how_to_apply: Open the International Q&A webinars page
Register for the November or December session
Join via Zoom at the scheduled time
Email international.admissions@admin.cam.ac.uk if you cannot attend

cambridge-virtual-postgraduate-open-days.about:
Cambridge's Virtual Postgraduate Open Days run entirely online. Week one (2–6 November 2026) has subject webinars from the University's six academic schools, from Arts and Humanities to Clinical Medicine, each a short presentation followed by Q&A with academics. Week two (9–13 November) covers the Colleges, funding opportunities and student support.

There are over 100 live sessions; you book the ones you want, and recordings are available to all registered attendees afterwards. It is the best single way for international applicants to research Cambridge Master's and PhD courses and scholarships (such as Gates Cambridge and Cambridge Trust awards) before the main funding deadlines.
highlights: Funding and College sessions in week two
cambridge-virtual-postgraduate-open-days.eligibility: Anyone considering postgraduate study at Cambridge, from any country.
how_to_apply: Open the Virtual Postgraduate Open Days page
Browse the programme by subject/day
Book the sessions you want
Attend live or watch the recordings

canada-jay-mathematical-competition-2026.about:
The CJMC is one of the CMS's open competitions alongside the COMC and the Canada Lynx competition. Schools register through the CMS portal, and students whose school is not participating can register independently. Outside Canada the fee is USD 15 per student (minimum 5).

It is a good confidence-building contest before harder olympiad-style papers.
highlights: Run by the Canadian Mathematical Society
canada-jay-mathematical-competition-2026.eligibility: Students (suggested grades 7–12) at participating schools anywhere, or independent students whose school is not participating.
how_to_apply: School registers on the CMS portal (or register as an independent student)
Register by 12 Nov and pay by 13 Nov 2026
Write the contest on 19/20 Nov 2026
canada-jay-mathematical-competition-2026.costs: CAD 12 per student in Canada; USD 15 per student outside Canada (minimum 5).

cattolica-milan-winter-programs-2027.about:
Università Cattolica del Sacro Cuore runs English-taught winter courses in Milan in January 2027, each with 44 contact hours and 6 ECTS. Courses: Personal Branding: Impact, Influence and Effectiveness in the Workplace (5–22 January), Entrepreneurship and Innovation (5–15 January), Business, Government and the Global Economy (5–15 January) and Green Management and Sustainability (18–29 January). Students can combine courses.

Applicants must be enrolled in higher education with at least two completed semesters, a GPA of about 2.75/4, and English at B2 (TOEFL iBT 79 / IELTS 6.0). Students can apply through a partner university or directly as free-movers.

Tuition is €1,550 for one course or €2,900 for two, plus a €75 application fee.
cattolica-milan-winter-programs-2027.eligibility: University students with at least two completed semesters, GPA ≈2.75/4 (or equivalent), English B2 (TOEFL iBT 79 / IELTS 6.0) if not native.
how_to_apply: Choose one or two January 2027 courses.
Apply via the partner-university or free-mover/direct application route.
Pay the €75 application fee.
Pay tuition and arrange housing in Milan.
cattolica-milan-winter-programs-2027.costs: Application fee €75; tuition €1,550 (one course) or €2,900 (two), including enrolment fee, 44 contact hours and orientation. Travel, housing and meals not included.

cbs-summer-university-2027.about:
CBS Summer University is one of Europe's largest business summer schools, at the triple-accredited (EQUIS, AMBA, AACSB) Copenhagen Business School. All courses start on 28 June 2027: 6-week courses (7.5 ECTS each, combine up to two for 15 ECTS) run to 6 August, intensive 3-week courses (7.5 ECTS) to 16 July, and 2-week courses (3 ECTS) to 9 July.

More than 50 bachelor's and master's courses cover classic business subjects plus entrepreneurship, globalisation, IT, innovation, psychology, supply chain and more. A social programme (Copenhagen tours, folk dancing, day trips) and CBS dorm housing are available for an extra fee.

International students from EU and non-EU countries, professionals and lifelong learners can apply 26 January – 13 April 2027 at cbs.dk/summer.
cbs-summer-university-2027.eligibility: International students (EU and non-EU), exchange students, freemovers, business professionals and lifelong learners; course-level prerequisites and English requirements apply.
how_to_apply: Choose 6-, 3- or 2-week course(s) from the CBS course catalogue.
Apply on cbs.dk/summer between 26 January and 13 April 2027 (route depends on your student category).
Pay tuition after admission.
Book CBS housing (from 25 June 2027) if needed.
cbs-summer-university-2027.costs: Tuition per course on the CBS fees/freemover pages; social programme and housing extra (social package was DKK 800 in 2025).

ccfs-sorbonne-summer-french-courses-2027.about:
The Cours de Civilisation Française de la Sorbonne (CCFS) is a private higher-education institution in Paris teaching French to international students. Its monthly summer courses in 2027 run 2–29 June, 1–29 July and 2–27 August. Options include General French (E10), General French and French Civilisation (E20, with lectures on French culture, history and literature) and Intensive French (E40), with a summer quarterly course (E60) as well.

Students are placed by level. Applicants must be at least 18 and hold a secondary-school diploma, so it suits gap-year students and university students alike.

The E20 course costs €1,350 per month, plus a €100 annual registration fee; a 30% deposit secures the place and admission is final once fully paid at least one month before the start.
highlights: Three monthly sessions to choose from
ccfs-sorbonne-summer-french-courses-2027.eligibility: Aged 18+ with a secondary-school diploma or certificate of completion; all levels (placement by level). Check visa rules for your nationality.
how_to_apply: Choose a session (June, July or August 2027) and course (E10, E20, E40).
Register online via the course page's 'Register' button.
Pay the 30% deposit and €100 registration fee.
Pay the balance at least one month before the start.
ccfs-sorbonne-summer-french-courses-2027.costs: E20 General French & Civilisation: €1,350 per month for 2027 sessions (course list also shows E10 €900, E40 €1,600, E60 quarterly €3,700); €100 annual registration fee; 30% deposit. Accommodation not included.

cepe-unam-spanish-courses-2027.about:
The Centro de Enseñanza para Extranjeros (CEPE) is UNAM's centre for teaching Spanish and Mexican culture to foreigners, one of the oldest programmes of its kind in Latin America. It offers Spanish courses from beginner to advanced, courses on Mexican culture (history, art, literature), teacher-training courses, diplomas, and the official SIELE and EXELEAA Spanish proficiency exams.

Courses run in sessions throughout the year according to CEPE's 2027 academic calendar, at Ciudad Universitaria (Mexico City), Polanco and the colonial town of Taxco. It suits school leavers, university students and anyone preparing to study in a Spanish-speaking country.
highlights: Spanish at every level at Mexico's national university
Mexican culture courses and SIELE exam centre
Campuses in Mexico City and Taxco
cepe-unam-spanish-courses-2027.eligibility: Foreign learners of Spanish (non-native speakers); typically young adults and adults. Check age rules for minors with CEPE.
how_to_apply: Check the CEPE 2027 academic calendar for session dates
Take a placement test or choose your level
Register and pay online or in person before the session starts
Arrange a Mexican visitor visa if needed
cepe-unam-spanish-courses-2027.costs: Paid courses; fees published by CEPE per course and session (lower for UNAM-affiliated students).

charles-causley-young-peoples-poetry-com.about:
Run by the trust that cares for poet Charles Causley's home in Launceston, the competition has three age categories (5–10, 11–15, 16–18). This year's theme, 'Heritage', invites young people to explore Cornish roots in partnership with English Heritage; prizes include free English Heritage membership.

Entries can come through schools, groups or individually, with a completed entry form.
highlights: Prize-giving at the Launceston Poetry Festival
charles-causley-young-peoples-poetry-com.eligibility: Young people aged 5–18 living in Cornwall.
how_to_apply: Read the rules of entry
Write your poem on 'Heritage'
Send it with the entry form by 31 Dec 2026

checkpoint-1-games-for-good-2027.about:
Checkpoint is a twice-yearly hackathon series for builders aged 13–18. Checkpoint 01's theme is Games for Good: make a game that does something beyond entertaining, such as teaching a hard concept, raising awareness of an issue, supporting a cause or being playable by people often left out. Any engine, language or platform is allowed, and AI tools may be used freely.

The event runs online from Friday 8 to Sunday 10 January 2027, starting with a recorded kickoff call, a Saturday workshop on scoping a finishable project and forum help all weekend. Cash and sponsor prizes are offered. Checkpoint is fiscally sponsored by The Hack Foundation (a US 501(c)(3)) with named adult advisors and a code of conduct.
highlights: Any engine: Scratch, Godot, Unity, HTML…
checkpoint-1-games-for-good-2027.eligibility: Anyone aged 13–18 anywhere in the world.
how_to_apply: Register on the official Devpost page
Join the organisers' Discord/discussion board to find teammates
Build your project during the hacking period
Submit code, demo video and description before the deadline

code-for-humanity-hackathon-2027.about:
Code for Humanity is a global online hackathon for students, developers, designers and changemakers who want to build technology for social good: disaster response, low-income and rural areas, people with disabilities, refugees, under-resourced schools, and regions with limited access to healthcare, education or financial services.

You can enter solo or in a team, and no prior experience is needed. Submit a working solution and a short demo video by 15 January 2027. There are no cash prizes, but every submission receives a certificate of participation.
code-for-humanity-hackathon-2027.eligibility: Anyone, anywhere; students and first-time builders welcome.
how_to_apply: Register on the official Devpost page
Join the organisers' Discord/discussion board to find teammates
Build your project during the hacking period
Submit code, demo video and description before the deadline

columbia-summer-session-visiting-student.about:
Columbia University's Summer Session lets visiting students from domestic and international universities take Columbia courses for credit in New York City over the summer. Courses span the arts and sciences, business-related subjects, languages and professional fields, taught by Columbia faculty, with options for summer housing on the Morningside Heights campus.

The Summer Session runs every year from about May to August in six-week sessions. Columbia advises international students to apply early because of longer visa processing times; 2027 calendars, deadlines, tuition and housing details are published on the Summer Session site.
highlights: Columbia courses for credit in New York
Open to students of international universities
columbia-summer-session-visiting-student.eligibility: Undergraduate, graduate and post-baccalaureate students enrolled at domestic or international universities; English proficiency required.
how_to_apply: Check the 2027 academic calendar and course list when published
Apply online as a visiting student (apply early for visa processing)
Request an I-20 for an F-1 visa if studying on campus
Register for courses and summer housing
columbia-summer-session-visiting-student.costs: Tuition per credit plus fees and optional housing, listed on the Tuition & Financing page.

cornell-precollege-summer-2027.about:
Cornell Precollege Studies lets high-school students enrol in regular Cornell undergraduate courses during the summer, earning 3 to 12 transferable credits on an official Cornell transcript. Students can live on Cornell's Ithaca campus (three- and six-week courses), commute, or study online; subjects include architecture, business, computer science, engineering, humanities and sciences.

Summer 2027 will offer three-, six- and eight-week options from June to August, with details published in December 2026 (a Winter 2027 online session also runs 4–22 January). Cornell reports precollege students from more than 50 countries and has offices to support international students.
highlights: Earn 3–12 Cornell credits and an official transcript
cornell-precollege-summer-2027.eligibility: High-school students (typically rising juniors and seniors and some younger students by course) from any country, with English proficiency. Online course access from some sanctioned regions needs special approval.
how_to_apply: Check Cornell Precollege pages in December 2026 for 2027 courses
Choose residential, commuter or online
Apply online with transcript and English proficiency evidence if needed
Pay tuition and housing; arrange a US visa for residential study
cornell-precollege-summer-2027.costs: Paid per credit plus housing and fees; 2027 costs published with the summer schedule.

cosmo-hacks-2026.about:
Cosmo Hacks is a free, fully online hackathon for middle-school, high-school and university students aged 13+. The 2026 theme is 'Tech for Student & Community Life': build an app, game, website, tool or experiment that solves one clear problem for students, schools or local communities. Work alone or in teams of up to four (same division); beginners are welcome.

Building runs from 19 December 2026 (10:00 am CST opening ceremony) to 18 January 2027 (4:00 pm CST), with workshops in the first days, mentor support on Discord, remote judging on 18–22 January and a closing ceremony on 23 January. Projects are scored on creativity, functionality, technical implementation, impact and presentation; there is a cash prize pool plus over USD 150,000 in sponsor benefits, and every participant receives a certificate.
cosmo-hacks-2026.eligibility: Students aged 13+ in middle school, high school or university, from any country. Teams of up to 4.
how_to_apply: Register on the official Devpost page
Join the organisers' Discord/discussion board to find teammates
Build your project during the hacking period
Submit code, demo video and description before the deadline

ctmun-fall-2026.about:
CTMUN is a long-running Central Texas conference, now holding its 32nd fall session, organised by University of Texas at Austin students at Westlake High School, with hundreds of delegates 'where Texas meets the world'.

The conference runs 7–8 November 2026 at Westlake High School (Austin area), United States. It is open to middle and high school students across Texas. Working language: English.

Use 'Register' on the official site. The delegate fee is published on the official registration page. As at any MUN, delegates research their assigned country, write position papers, give speeches, negotiate in caucuses and draft resolutions — hands-on training in public speaking, research and diplomacy that universities value.
highlights: Run by UT Austin students; 32nd fall session
The delegate fee is published on the official registration page
ctmun-fall-2026.eligibility: Open to middle and high school students across Texas. Working language: English. No nationality restrictions are stated; international delegates (including from Georgia and Qatar) can apply, arranging their own visa and travel.
how_to_apply: Open the official website (link below) and read the conference information and committee list.
Use 'Register' on the official site.
Pay the delegate fee by the stated deadline to confirm your place.
Prepare a position paper using the committee study guides before the conference.
ctmun-fall-2026.costs: The delegate fee is published on the official registration page. Travel, accommodation and visas are paid by participants unless stated otherwise.

cubes-in-space-2026-27.about:
Cubes in Space describes itself as the only global STEM programme giving students aged 11–18 suborbital flight opportunities on NASA missions. Students, usually guided by a teacher, design and build an experiment that fits inside a small cube, which is launched on a sounding rocket or research balloon from NASA's Wallops Flight Facility. Since 2014 around 28,000 students from 79 countries have taken part.

The programme includes an online student academy with learning modules, and selected experiments fly in summer and are returned to the teams for analysis. Registration and enrolment for 2026–27 open on 9 November 2026; the detailed timeline is on the official site. Note: the programme does not fly cubesats or nanosats.
highlights: Your experiment flies on a NASA mission
cubes-in-space-2026-27.eligibility: Students aged 11–18 worldwide, typically registered through a teacher or educator.
how_to_apply: Check the official timeline on cubesinspace.com
Register when enrolment opens on 9 Nov 2026 (usually via a teacher)
Complete the online student academy and design your experiment
Submit the experiment proposal by the programme deadline
cubes-in-space-2026-27.costs: No fee is listed on the official site; teams cover their own materials and shipping.

czech-summer-schools-slavonic-studies-sc.about:
The Summer Schools of Slavonic Studies (SSSS) are three- to four-week Czech language courses held every July and August at Charles University (Prague and Poděbrady), Masaryk University (Brno), Palacký University (Olomouc), the University of West Bohemia (Pilsen) and the University of South Bohemia (České Budějovice). Levels run from absolute beginner (A0) to C1, with lectures on Czech culture and history and excursions; teaching is in Czech or via English depending on your level.

The Czech Ministry of Education offers scholarships that cover tuition plus board and lodging in student dormitories. In 2026 citizens of about 40 countries could apply, including Georgia; Qatar is not on the list. Candidates must be at least 18, be students or graduates (or academics in Czech/Slavic studies), and must first be selected and nominated by their country's nominating institution before registering in the ministry's online system.
highlights: Tuition, accommodation and meals covered by the Czech government
Six university summer schools, all levels A0–C1
Georgia is among the eligible countries
czech-summer-schools-slavonic-studies-sc.eligibility: Aged 18+, university students or graduates (priority to students, teachers, translators and scholars of Czech/Slavic studies) who are citizens of an eligible country; Georgia was eligible in 2026. Must be nominated by the national nominating institution (e.g. the Czech Embassy). Qatar not listed.
how_to_apply: Contact the nominating institution in your country (for Georgia, the Czech Embassy in Tbilisi) in early 2027 and ask for its deadline
Submit its application form and any documents it requires
If nominated, register in the Czech Ministry's online system and complete the scholarship application in Czech or English
Choose only from the summer schools allocated to your country
Arrange travel and compulsory travel medical insurance
czech-summer-schools-slavonic-studies-sc.costs: Scholarship covers tuition and board and lodging in a student dormitory. Not covered: international travel and insurance (non-EU citizens must buy travel medical insurance).

destination-imagination-global-finals-20.about:
Destination Imagination teams of students choose one of the season's challenges (technical, scientific, fine arts, improvisational, engineering, service learning) and spend months designing a solution, which they present at an Affiliate Tournament together with an 'Instant Challenge' solved on the spot. Top-ranked teams are invited to Global Finals, which bring together teams from around the world.

Teams register through their regional or national affiliate; there is also a Team Film Challenge (September–December) that can be done remotely.
destination-imagination-global-finals-20.eligibility: Student teams from elementary to university level registered with DI, competing through their affiliate (teams from China are not eligible for the waitlist route).
how_to_apply: Start a team with an adult team manager
Register with DI and your affiliate
Choose a challenge and develop your solution
Rank at your Affiliate Tournament to qualify
destination-imagination-global-finals-20.costs: Team registration and tournament fees; Global Finals travel self-funded.

doshisha-womens-college-japanese-immersi.about:
Doshisha Women's College of Liberal Arts runs a small Japanese Language Immersion Course at its Imadegawa campus in central Kyoto. Term A runs 17 May – 11 June 2027 and Term B 21 June – 16 July 2027; you can take one or both.

Each week has ten 90-minute morning Japanese classes at two levels, plus cultural experiences (tea ceremony, calligraphy, kimono), Kyoto field trips and social events with Japanese students. With a maximum of 10 students per term, teaching is very personal. No credits are awarded.

It is for female undergraduates or graduates aged 18+ with at least six months of Japanese. Apply 5 January – 18 February 2027.
highlights: ¥60,000 grants for partner and ASEAN students
doshisha-womens-college-japanese-immersi.eligibility: Female undergraduate students or graduates of a higher-education institution abroad, aged 18+ on 1 April 2027, with at least 6 months of Japanese study.
how_to_apply: Download the application forms from the course page.
Email documents to the Division of International Affairs (directly or via your university) between 5 Jan and 18 Feb 2027.
Pay fees by the end of March 2027.
Arrange a visa if needed.
doshisha-womens-college-japanese-immersi.costs: ¥139,600 per term (tuition, field trips, parties, insurance); dormitory ¥54,000 (one term) or ¥106,500 (both). Grants of ¥60,000 per term for affiliated-institution and ASEAN students.

dsh-hacks-v2-2026.about:
DSH Hacks V2 is a global online competition for students aged 13+, co-hosted by three youth-led organisations (DeltaForge Hacks, NXT Horizon and STEMise). The theme is AI x Healthcare: identify a real healthcare problem and build a technical solution, from diagnostic tools and patient-care platforms to AI systems for detecting or managing illness.

Submissions need a working prototype with user interaction (hardware allowed with code), a demo video, a one-page PDF description and the code repository. Use of AI tools is encouraged. Prizes are non-cash (software credits, memberships, gift cards). The submission window closes on 15 November 2026.
highlights: Theme: AI for real healthcare problems
how_to_apply: Register on the official Devpost page
Join the organisers' Discord/discussion board to find teammates
Build your project during the hacking period
Submit code, demo video and description before the deadline

durham-global-gateway-series-2026.about:
Durham University's Global Gateway Series is a set of virtual open-day events for prospective undergraduate and postgraduate students around the world. From 23 to 27 November 2026 you can build your own programme from a wide range of online sessions: subject-specific presentations led by academics, guidance on the application process, an introduction to Durham's collegiate system, and sessions with current students.

All sessions run in UK time, with some repeated to suit other time zones. Durham also promotes its application-based partial scholarship for international students starting in 2027/28 and its Global Futures pre-university summer school (July 2027).
highlights: Choose from many subject and college sessions
Repeated sessions for different time zones
durham-global-gateway-series-2026.eligibility: Prospective undergraduate and postgraduate students from any country.
how_to_apply: Open the Global Gateway Series page
Use the booking form to pick sessions
Receive joining links by email
Attend between 23 and 27 Nov 2026

dutch-informatics-olympiad-2027.about:
The NIO first round is a take-home set of programming tasks that students can work on at their own pace and submit online. Qualifiers attend the second round in Enschede (March 2027), then final training in Baarn and the national final (June 2027). The Dutch team competes at WEOI (Spain), EGOI (Poland) and IOI 2027 (Germany).

Tasks and the submission system are online; the competition is free.
dutch-informatics-olympiad-2027.eligibility: Secondary-school students in the Netherlands (check the site for exact eligibility).
how_to_apply: Download the round-1 tasks from informaticaolympiade.nl
Write your solutions
Submit before 21 Jan 2027
Qualify for round 2 in March

em-strasbourg-summer-school-2027.about:
EM Strasbourg Business School's Summer School runs 11–25 June 2027 in Strasbourg, home of the European Parliament and the Council of Europe. The core course, Business in Europe, covers Responsible Leadership for a Sustainable Europe and Understanding Europe, worth 6 ECTS (3 US credits).

Visits have included the European Parliament, the Council of Europe, Mercedes-Benz and Weberhaus, alongside cultural activities (wine tour, cheese tasting, cooking workshop). The fee covers tuition, corporate visits, cultural activities and welcome/farewell lunches; housing in student residences is about €300–350.

Open to undergraduates with at least one year of higher education (business or economics basics) and English B2. Apply by 15 March 2027.
highlights: Visits to EU institutions in Strasbourg
em-strasbourg-summer-school-2027.eligibility: Undergraduates with at least one year of higher education and basic business/economics knowledge; other disciplines welcome; English B2. No French needed.
how_to_apply: Partner students: wait for your university's nomination (links sent in November).
Non-partner students: email summer.school@em-strasbourg.eu.
Apply by 15 March 2027.
Pay fees and book student housing.
em-strasbourg-summer-school-2027.costs: Fee on request from summer.school@em-strasbourg.eu (covers tuition, visits, cultural activities, some meals). Housing about €300–350, paid by students.

emory-pre-college-program-2027.about:
Emory Pre-College offers two-week, non-credit courses taught by Emory faculty and graduate students in subjects ranging from neuroscience, medicine and psychology to creative writing, business and law. Residential students live in Emory dorms in Atlanta and join social and cultural activities; Emory also runs a separate Pre-Med Institute and a credit-bearing Summer College.

In 2027 the Pre-College sessions run 13–26 June, 27 June–10 July and 11–24 July. The programme is for current high-school sophomores and juniors. Applications open in December 2026 and close on 3 May 2027 (popular courses fill earlier). Anyone who is not a US citizen or permanent resident applies as an international applicant, with English proficiency shown by SAT/ACT scores, TOEFL 104 / IELTS 7.5 or a competitive Duolingo score, plus a writing sample.
emory-pre-college-program-2027.eligibility: Current high-school sophomores and juniors. International applicants welcome; English proficiency required (SAT ERW 700+, ACT English 30+, TOEFL iBT 104, IELTS 7.5 or competitive Duolingo score) plus an English writing sample.
how_to_apply: Choose a session and course when 2027 courses are published
Apply online from December 2026 (USD 70 fee)
International applicants: upload English test score and writing sample
Submit before 3 May 2027 (earlier for popular courses)
Pay tuition and arrange a US visa once admitted
emory-pre-college-program-2027.costs: Paid programme; tuition and housing listed on Emory's Costs & Scholarships page. USD 70 non-refundable application fee. Some scholarships available.

emory-pre-med-institute-2027.about:
The Emory Pre-Med Institute is one of Emory's three summer offerings for high-school students (alongside two-week Pre-College courses and credit-bearing Summer College). It gives students considering medicine a structured introduction to health sciences and medical careers at a university known for its medical school and hospital system, with a daily schedule of classes and activities and residential life on Emory's Atlanta campus.

The 2027 institute runs 13 June–3 July. Applications open in December 2026 and close on 1 February 2027. Applicants who are not US citizens or permanent residents apply as international applicants and show English proficiency (for example TOEFL iBT 104, IELTS 7.5, SAT ERW 700+ or ACT English 30+) and submit a writing sample; the application fee is USD 70.
highlights: Focused introduction to medicine and health careers
Hosted by a university with a major medical school
emory-pre-med-institute-2027.eligibility: High-school students (Emory Pre-College targets current sophomores and juniors). International applicants accepted with English test scores and a writing sample.
how_to_apply: Apply online from December 2026 (USD 70 fee)
Upload transcript, essays and, for international applicants, English test and writing sample
Submit by 1 February 2027
If admitted, pay tuition and arrange a US visa
emory-pre-med-institute-2027.costs: Paid residential programme; costs on Emory's Costs & Scholarships page. Application fee USD 70.

emory-summer-college-2027.about:
Emory Summer College lets advanced high-school students enrol in regular Emory undergraduate summer courses taught by Emory faculty and earn transferable college credit. It is the most academically demanding of Emory's three summer programmes for high-school students.

In 2027 Session 1 runs 11 May–17 June (apply by 20 April) and Session 2 runs 28 June–4 August (apply by 7 June). Applications open in December 2026. International applicants apply with English proficiency evidence (TOEFL iBT 104 / IELTS 7.5 or SAT/ACT equivalents) and a writing sample.
highlights: Two sessions with spring and summer deadlines
emory-summer-college-2027.eligibility: Academically strong high-school students (typically rising juniors and seniors). International applicants accepted with English proficiency evidence and a writing sample.
how_to_apply: Choose Session 1 or 2 and your courses
Apply online from December 2026 (USD 70 fee)
Submit English test and writing sample if international
Meet the session deadline (20 April or 7 June 2027)
emory-summer-college-2027.costs: Paid per credit hour plus housing; details on Emory's Costs & Scholarships page. Application fee USD 70.

estonia-ekkav-language-course-scholarshi.about:
The EKKAV programme (Estonian Language and Culture Academic Studies abroad) offers scholarships for international university students to attend Estonian language and culture summer and winter courses in Estonia, such as the Tallinn University winter course. The scholarship covers the course participation fee, accommodation and the cultural excursions of the course; travel is self-funded.

Applicants must be enrolled at a foreign university (BA, MA or PhD) and be studying or have studied Estonian. You register for the course yourself and send Harno a signed application describing the value of the course to you, with a recommendation from your Estonian lecturer or other proof of your Estonian. The current round is open until 15 November 2026.
highlights: Covers course fee, accommodation and excursions
Winter and summer Estonian language courses in Estonia
Short application: motivation statement plus lecturer's recommendation
estonia-ekkav-language-course-scholarshi.eligibility: Students enrolled at a non-Estonian university (bachelor's, master's or PhD) who are studying or have previously studied Estonian. Any nationality.
how_to_apply: Choose an Estonian language summer or winter course and register for it yourself
Download the EKKAV application form from Harno's page
Sign the form digitally or by hand and scan it
Email it with a recommendation from your Estonian lecturer (or proof of Estonian) to Harno by 15 November 2026, subject 'Suve- ja talvekursuste stipendium (EKKAV)'
estonia-ekkav-language-course-scholarshi.costs: Scholarship covers the course participation fee, accommodation and cultural excursions. Travel to Estonia is paid by the student.

ewha-international-summer-college-2027.about:
The Ewha International Summer College (EISC) is run by Ewha Womans University's Office of International Affairs and is open to students of all genders. Session 1 (about four weeks) lets fee-paying visiting students take one or two 3-credit courses (45 hours each), taught in English, plus Korean language at four levels; Session 2 is a shorter August session. Optional housing and field trips are available.

It is open to undergraduate and graduate students at accredited universities (minimum GPA 2.0/4.0) and to prospective freshmen already admitted to college. Credits are transcripted by Ewha; transfer depends on your home institution.
highlights: Early-bird discount; optional dorm and field trips
ewha-international-summer-college-2027.eligibility: Undergraduate or graduate students at an accredited university (cumulative GPA at least 2.0/4.0) and admitted freshmen. All nationalities.
how_to_apply: Check summer.ewha.ac.kr for 2027 dates and courses
Apply online with passport bio page and transcript/admission proof
Pay the KRW 100,000 application fee (and tuition early for the early-bird discount)
Pay tuition and housing after acceptance; Session 1 deadline about mid-May
ewha-international-summer-college-2027.costs: 2026: application fee KRW 100,000; tuition KRW 1,800,000 (1 course) or 3,000,000 (2 courses) in Session 1, with early-bird reductions; dormitory KRW 730,000–1,300,000; optional field trip about KRW 450,000.

ewha-international-winter-college-2026-2.about:
Ewha International Winter College (EIWC) is the winter session of Ewha Womans University in Seoul, open to international students of all genders (male students are housed at I-House). Classes run 28 December 2026 – 11 January 2027, with orientation on 24 December.

Students take one or two English-taught courses or Korean language, with optional field trips around Korea.

Tuition is KRW 1,600,000 for one course or KRW 2,500,000 for two, plus a KRW 100,000 application fee; room-only housing costs KRW 550,000–1,100,000. Apply and pay tuition by 30 November 2026.
ewha-international-winter-college-2026-2.eligibility: University students worldwide (see EIWC eligibility on the site).
how_to_apply: Check the course list.
Apply online and pay the KRW 100,000 fee.
Pay tuition by 30 November 2026.
Pay housing and field-trip fees in December.
ewha-international-winter-college-2026-2.costs: Application KRW 100,000; tuition KRW 1,600,000 (1 course) or KRW 2,500,000 (2 courses); housing KRW 550,000–1,100,000 (room only). Re-enrolment 50% discount.

fermun-2027.about:
FerMUN, organised since 2012 by the public Lycée international de Ferney-Voltaire, is a multilingual Model UN held inside real UN buildings in Geneva — the ITU headquarters and the Palais des Nations. Hundreds of lycée students debate, negotiate and run a student newsroom.

The conference runs 5–8 January 2027 at the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) headquarters and the United Nations Office at Geneva, Switzerland. It is open to upper-secondary (lycée) students from the organising and invited schools. Working language: French and English (multilingual).

Schools register via 'Inscription' on the official site; topics, committees and country allocations for 2027 are already published. The delegate fee is published on the official registration page. As at any MUN, delegates research their assigned country, write position papers, give speeches, negotiate in caucuses and draft resolutions — hands-on training in public speaking, research and diplomacy that universities value.
highlights: Held inside the Palais des Nations and ITU
The delegate fee is published on the official registration page
fermun-2027.eligibility: Open to upper-secondary (lycée) students from the organising and invited schools. Working language: French and English (multilingual). No nationality restrictions are stated; international delegates (including from Georgia and Qatar) can apply, arranging their own visa and travel.
how_to_apply: Open the official website (link below) and read the conference information and committee list.
Schools register via 'Inscription' on the official site; topics, committees and country allocations for 2027 are already published.
Pay the delegate fee by the stated deadline to confirm your place.
Prepare a position paper using the committee study guides before the conference.
fermun-2027.costs: The delegate fee is published on the official registration page. Travel, accommodation and visas are paid by participants unless stated otherwise.

fudan-international-summer-session-2027.about:
Fudan International Summer Session (FISS) is a four-week English-taught programme for college students from around the world, held since 2012 with more than 7,000 participants. Content courses cover business and economy, history and culture, science and technology, society and politics, medicine and law; students can also take Chinese language at several levels and PE courses such as Chinese kung fu and folk dance, and study alongside Fudan degree students.

Activities include a campus tour, Shanghai city exploration, a Huangpu River cruise, company visits, dragon and lion dance and calligraphy. Participants receive a programme certificate and an official Fudan transcript. In 2026 tuition was a flat CNY 22,000 for up to 6 credits plus PE and Chinese, and Fudan offered no scholarships.
highlights: Up to 6 Fudan credits plus Chinese language
Courses across business, culture, science, politics, medicine and law
Shanghai cultural programme and company visits
fudan-international-summer-session-2027.eligibility: College/university students aged 18+ with sufficient English proficiency and in good health. All nationalities (UC students via UCEAP).
how_to_apply: Watch iss.fudan.edu.cn for the 2027 session announcement
Apply on Fudan's online application system and pay the CNY 400 fee
After admission, pay tuition and enrol in courses
Arrange accommodation and a Chinese visa
fudan-international-summer-session-2027.costs: 2026: application fee CNY 400; tuition CNY 22,000 flat (CNY 19,800 for partner-nominated students; tuition waived for nominated exchange students). Accommodation, insurance and travel extra. No Fudan scholarships in 2026.

fudan-international-winter-session-2026-.about:
Fudan University's International Winter Session is an annual three-week English-taught study programme for college students from around the world, held on Fudan's Shanghai campus from 21 December 2026 to 8 January 2027. Students take 2-credit content courses such as International Trade, China's Modern Economy, Corporate Finance, Artificial Intelligence in FinTech and Social Networks and Chinese Society, and can add Chinese language. The fee includes cultural activities and a company visit.

The programme is open to university students with sufficient English. Applications close on 9 November 2026 for non-Chinese applicants, so act quickly. Accommodation is not included (Fudan provides an off-campus housing list), and Fudan is not offering scholarships for its 2026 sessions.
highlights: Fudan credits in English-taught courses on China, business and AI
Chinese language option, company visit and cultural activities
fudan-international-winter-session-2026-.eligibility: College/university students of any nationality with sufficient English and in good health. Applicants of Chinese nationality apply through a separate route.
how_to_apply: Create an account on Fudan's online application system and select the 2026 Fudan International Winter Session (self-paying)
Upload the required documents and submit by 11:00 Beijing time, 9 November 2026
Pay the CNY 400 application fee
After admission, pay tuition by 7 December 2026 and arrange housing and an X2/visa as instructed
fudan-international-winter-session-2026-.costs: Application fee CNY 400; tuition CNY 18,000 (early-bird CNY 16,200 has passed), including courses, cultural activities and company visit. Accommodation, insurance and travel not included. No Fudan scholarships in 2026.

georg-mohr-konkurrencen-2026-27.about:
The Georg Mohr Competition is held in Danish upper-secondary schools. Round 1 is sat at school; the best students go on to round 2, and the top performers are invited to training for international olympiads (in 2026 Denmark won a bronze medal at the IMO).

Teachers register their schools; materials and a teacher info pack for 2027 are on the site.
highlights: Path to IMO, EGMO and Baltic Way
georg-mohr-konkurrencen-2026-27.eligibility: Students at upper-secondary schools in Denmark (younger strong students may also participate).
how_to_apply: Ask your maths teacher to register the school
Practise with past round-1 problems
Sit round 1 at school on 24 Nov 2026

georgia-state-summer-institute-2027.about:
The Georgia State University Summer Institute is designed for international college students who want a month of US university study. Participants take courses worth 6 credits (charged at in-state tuition), live in university housing in downtown Atlanta, and join excursions around the city and region.

The 2027 programme runs 30 June–31 July (classes 6–24 July, finals 27 July). The USD 5,900 fee covers tuition and fees for 6 credits, 31 nights of housing in shared rooms, a full meal plan, excursion admissions and local transport; flights, visa fees and insurance (about USD 140) are extra. Applicants must be at least 17 by the start date. Applications open in November and close 15 March; a USD 450 deposit is due by 22 March or within a week of acceptance.
highlights: All-inclusive fee with housing and meals
georgia-state-summer-institute-2027.eligibility: International college-level students aged 17+ by 30 June 2027 (born before 30 June 2010). English proficiency required.
how_to_apply: Choose courses from the Summer Institute course list
Apply online from November 2026 by 15 March 2027
Pay the USD 450 deposit within one week of acceptance
Obtain your US visa with the university's documents
Pay the balance and housing fee by 15 May 2027
georgia-state-summer-institute-2027.costs: USD 5,900 all-inclusive (6 credits, housing, meals, excursions, local transport); insurance about USD 140; flights and visa extra.

global-nomads-language-exchange-classes.about:
Global Nomads Group's Building Understanding through Language Learning programme is a virtual exchange for middle- and high-school students learning English, Arabic or Spanish. Two tracks exist: English–Arabic and English–Spanish. Students complete four short self-paced modules built by young people (story exchanges, multimedia, real-life language) and join two live, facilitated bilingual sessions where they practise with peers who speak the language they are learning.

It lasts five weeks (about 4 hours of modules and 2 hours of live events), fits into normal class time, and students earn a certificate of completion. Teachers receive training and technical support, and the schedule is arranged with them. It is a natural fit for Arabic-speaking schools whose students are learning English.
highlights: Live bilingual sessions with peers abroad
global-nomads-language-exchange-classes.eligibility: Middle- and high-school classes learning English, Arabic or Spanish; a teacher must register the class.
how_to_apply: Ask your English/Arabic/Spanish teacher to open the programme page
Teacher registers the class with the free form
Attend the orientation and schedule sessions with Global Nomads staff
Complete the modules and the two live exchanges

global-nomads-village-virtual-impact-lab.about:
Village Virtual Impact Lab is a fellowship run by Global Nomads Group, a nonprofit that has designed virtual cross-cultural programmes for young people since 1998. Each cycle has 32 fellows working in teams of eight from different countries; each team receives a brief from a real mission-driven NGO (environment, human rights, health, education and more), builds what it needs and presents it to the client.

The programme runs for 16 weeks from January 2027, with a live two-hour session most Saturdays (training workshops and team work) plus 2–4 hours of independent work per week, coaching from a Global Nomads coach, a certificate and letters on completion. Acceptance is selective (around 10% in past cohorts) but based on motivation rather than grades. It was designed for unstable internet and is accessible to neurodivergent learners and people with disabilities.
highlights: Real NGO project with an international team
Weekly live training and a personal coach
Financial aid for at least half of fellows (incl. devices/internet)
global-nomads-village-virtual-impact-lab.eligibility: Young people aged 16–24 (as of January 2027) anywhere in the world. No experience needed; English is the working language.
how_to_apply: Open the Village page and start the application
Complete the written part and record a short video
Request financial aid in the application if needed
Submit by 7 Dec 2026 (rolling review)
global-nomads-village-virtual-impact-lab.costs: USD 3,500 for the full 16 weeks (training, coaching, certificate). Financial aid is available and can cover the full cost, devices and internet.

google-buildhybridai-2026.about:
#BuildHybridAI 2026 is a Google/Firebase developer challenge on Devpost. Participants build AI-powered apps using Firebase AI Logic hybrid inference, which lets the same app run models on-device or in the cloud. Registration is open now; full rules, judging criteria, prizes and bonus challenges are released when submissions open on 9 November 2026.

You have three weeks to build (until 30 November 2026, 2:00 pm PT), solo or in a team, competing for USD 10,000 in cash prizes. A good portfolio project for university computer-science students.
highlights: Build with Firebase and on-device AI
google-buildhybridai-2026.eligibility: Developers who meet the official rules (published 9 Nov 2026; Google challenges usually require the age of majority and exclude sanctioned countries).
how_to_apply: Register on the official Devpost page
Join the organisers' Discord/discussion board to find teammates
Build your project during the hacking period
Submit code, demo video and description before the deadline

granada-clm-summer-spanish-language-cult.about:
The University of Granada's Centro de Lenguas Modernas (CLM), one of Spain's leading Spanish-as-a-foreign-language centres, runs a Summer Course in Spanish Language and Culture in 2027: June (2–29 June, 90 hours), July (2–29 July, 90 hours) or both (180 hours).

Students at B1.1–C2 level build a 90-hour timetable from language and culture subjects; at B2.2+ they can choose company-internship or healthcare-centre internship subjects. A placement test is held the working day before the course starts. Granada, home of the Alhambra, is a classic student city.

The fee is €1,395 per 90-hour course (€2,664 for June + July), with a lower early-period price shown on the page. Register via the official course page.
highlights: Study in the city of the Alhambra
granada-clm-summer-spanish-language-cult.eligibility: Learners of Spanish at B1.1 or above (internship subjects need B2.2+); see CLM general conditions.
how_to_apply: Read the 2027 course page.
Register via the #inscripcion section of the official page.
Take the placement test (1 June or 1 July).
Book accommodation through CLM's service if needed.
granada-clm-summer-spanish-language-cult.costs: €1,395 per 90-hour course; €2,664 for June + July (early-period prices lower). Accommodation not included.

green-shift-hacks-2026.about:
Green Shift Hacks is an online student hackathon for technology that makes sustainable choices easier, clearer and more scalable. Projects can focus on energy, waste, water, food, transport, materials, ecosystems or climate resilience, and must include a working prototype.

Submit a Devpost project page with your story, team, a demo video and source code, explaining the problem, users, approach and expected environmental benefit. Judging emphasises environmental impact. Submissions close on 17 November 2026.
green-shift-hacks-2026.eligibility: Students worldwide; check the Devpost rules for age limits.
how_to_apply: Register on the official Devpost page
Join the organisers' Discord/discussion board to find teammates
Build your project during the hacking period
Submit code, demo video and description before the deadline

groningen-islas-spring-school-faroe-2027.about:
ISLAS (Islands as Lighthouses for Sustainability) is a University of Groningen school held in person in Tórshavn, Faroe Islands, on 4–7 May 2027. It covers island studies: place-based identities, belonging and social inclusion, human and non-human relations including the sea and climate, connectivity and infrastructure, mobilities and migration, and ethics in small-island research.

It is designed for PhD students and research master's students, who submit a pre-course project outline; full attendance and group work are required. The certificate lists a 140-hour workload (about 5 ECTS).

The fee of €450 includes lunches, refreshments and an excursion. Apply with CV, motivation letter and transcript by 20 December 2026 (rolling selection).
groningen-islas-spring-school-faroe-2027.eligibility: PhD students and research master's students; English sufficient for discussion; pre-course project outline required.
how_to_apply: Prepare CV (max 2 pages), motivation letter (1 page) and transcript.
Apply online by 20 December 2026 (rolling).
Submit the pre-course project outline.
Book flights and accommodation.
groningen-islas-spring-school-faroe-2027.costs: €450 including lunches, refreshments and excursion; flights and accommodation not included.
